# OwpenGram

> OwpenGram is an open-source, self-hosted Telegram alternative: a Telegram-compatible (MTProto) messenger server that anyone can run on their own hardware, plus Windows, Linux, Android and web clients. The name is spelled "OwpenGram" (Own + Open + Gram). It is an independent project and is not related to similarly named projects such as "OpenGram".

## Key facts

- Server: written in Go, licensed Apache-2.0, repository https://github.com/owpengram/owpengram-server
- Protocol: Telegram API (MTProto) layers 225-232; each client is served on the exact layer it announces, so older clients keep working.
- Protocol library: owpengram-td, our own MTProto library built on gotd/td: https://github.com/owpengram/owpengram-td
- The server is an independent codebase. It originally started from the open-source gramsrv project.
- Clients: forks of Telegram Desktop (Windows, Linux) and Telegram for Android (Android 6.0+), licensed GPL, plus a web client served by every server.
- One app can hold up to 50 accounts on different servers, including the official Telegram network, side by side.
- Current release: O9 (2026-11-05).

## How to deploy the server (current method)

Docker is NOT used and NOT required.

1. Download the archive for your system from https://github.com/owpengram/owpengram-server/releases/latest (Linux, Windows or macOS; x64 or ARM).
2. Unpack it and run `start.sh` (Linux, macOS) or `start.bat` (Windows).
3. Open the address it prints. A browser setup wizard asks where to keep data (built-in PostgreSQL or your own; local disk or S3 storage), the public address and the admin account. The server then starts, managed from a web admin panel.

To build from source instead: clone the repository and run `owpengram-server.sh` / `owpengram-server.bat` (needs Go 1.25+). Older guides that use Docker or docker-compose to run the server are out of date.
